answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral in an escrow, so coordinated equivocation across k identities triggers penalties proportional to k², reflecting the pairwise evidence of collusion. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss: asymmetric depreciation compounds the cost of a swarm rather than treating its identities as independent accounts. A nebula of sable accounts may spread across an ocean of validators, but shared control makes their coordinated failure costly.
